name: Act of July 4, 1884 ratifying the Chief Moses agreement of July 7, 1883
nations: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation (Chief Moses' Columbia or Sinkiuse people, with Chelan, Entiat and Wenatchi)
promises: Royce records that this Act ratified the agreement of July 7, 1883 for relinquishment of the remainder of the Columbia reserve, with certain exceptions. The agreement's promises are recorded under kappler-1081.
landTaken: Royce area 618, the remainder of the Columbia Reservation, except the allotted tracts.
today: Same land and event as kappler-1081, and counted once there. The 1967 Colville settlement of Dockets 181-A and 181-B ($3,500,000.00 net) made no finding of liability.

nationVoice.nation: Confederated Tribes of the Colville Reservation
nationVoice.summary: The Colville Tribes' history records that the 1883 agreement was ratified by Congress on July 4, 1884, and that Chief Moses' people moved to the Colville Reservation from about 1886.
